html:
A mission sent by Pope Gregory the Great to convert the Anglo-Saxons of England. About 40 monks led by Augustine, prior of Gregory's monastery in Rome, landed in Kent in 597.

After the end of Roman rule, pagan Anglo-Saxon settlers had taken over most of lowland Britain, while Christianity lived on among the Britons in the west and the Irish. King Æthelberht of Kent had a Christian Frankish wife, Bertha, and welcomed the monks; he was soon baptised. Augustine became the first Archbishop of Canterbury, a see that still heads the Church of England.

Progress was slow. Some kingdoms fell back to paganism, and Irish monks from Iona converted much of the north. At the Synod of Whitby in 664, Northumbria chose Roman customs over Irish ones. The mission tied England to Rome for nine centuries, until Henry VIII broke away, and brought Latin learning and church law. Its story was told by the monk Bede.
sum: A mission sent by Pope Gregory the Great to convert the Anglo-Saxons of England. About 40 monks led by Augustine, prior of Gregory's monastery in Rome, landed in Kent in 597.
